precepts.text: He is coming back with vengeance to defend us.
precepts.point: The Lord hear thee in the day of trouble; the name of the God of Jacob defend thee; send thee help from the sanctuary and strengthen thee out of Zion. When the time comes Christ is jumping down from heaven like he did in Egypt; we have to visualize this because it is a prophecy that will come true.

note.label: Psalm 20: The Lord Defends His Anointed

precepts.why:
“Send thee help from the sanctuary, and strengthen thee out of Zion”. Here is what that help looked like in Egypt: “For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course, Thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction”.

“And brought thine unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.” The Almighty word leaped down as a fierce man of war and filled all things with death.

When the time comes, Christ is jumping down from heaven like he did in Egypt. He is coming back with vengeance to defend us. We have to visualize this, because it is a prophecy that will come true: the name of the God of Jacob defending us in the day of trouble.

precepts.text: Behold the Lord's hand is not shortened that it cannot save, but your iniquities have separated between you and your God; that is the problem we face, not that his hand is short. Once we get right as a nation he will fight for us and get a name for himself.
precepts.point: Now know I that the Lord saveth his anointed; he will hear him from his holy heaven with the saving strength of his right hand. This is why we ask, to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed; his arm is not short, it can save.

note.label: Psalm 20: The Lord Defends His Anointed

precepts.why:
“Now know I that the Lord saveth his anointed; he will hear him from his holy heaven with the saving strength of his right hand.” This is why we ask, to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? “Behold, the Lord’s hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear”.

His arm is not short; it can save. The problem is on our side: “But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.” That is the problem we face, not that his hand is short.

Once we get right as a nation, he will fight for us and get a name for himself, saving his anointed with the saving strength of his right hand.

precepts.text: Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help and stay on horses and trust in chariots, but they look not unto the Holy One of Israel; you trust and get comfortable in captivity, in America's army, thinking destruction is not coming to this place.
precepts.point: Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we will remember the name of the Lord our God. Like today we trust in the shadow of Egypt still doing it; but we Israelites do not trust in oppression, we remember our God.

note.label: Psalm 20: The Lord Defends His Anointed

precepts.why:
“Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the Lord our God.” Isaiah pronounces the woe on the ones trusting in chariots: “Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the Lord!”

Like today, we trust in the shadow of Egypt, still doing it. You trust and get comfortable in captivity, in America's army, thinking destruction is not coming to this place, and you look not unto the Holy One of Israel. But we Israelites do not trust in oppression; we remember our God.

precepts.text: Because ye despise this word and trust in oppression and perverseness and stay thereon; you trust in the white man's word that a woman can wear pants and be over the man, though the Most High never said it, and you trust in their perverseness.
precepts.point: Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we will remember the name of the Lord our God. Like today we trust in the shadow of Egypt still doing it; but we Israelites do not trust in oppression, we remember our God.

note.label: Psalm 20: The Lord Defends His Anointed

precepts.why:
“Wherefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel, Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and stay thereon”. Trusting in chariots and horses is trusting in oppression and perverseness and staying on it, while despising the word.

You trust in the white man's word that a woman can wear pants and be over the man, though the Most High never said it, and you trust in their perverseness. Israelites do not trust in oppression; we remember the name of the Lord our God.

precepts.text: Now the Egyptians are men and not God, and their horses flesh and not spirit; the white man is just a man, he is not God, and their army has nothing on God's army.
precepts.point: Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we will remember the name of the Lord our God. Like today we trust in the shadow of Egypt still doing it; but we Israelites do not trust in oppression, we remember our God.

note.label: Psalm 20: The Lord Defends His Anointed

precepts.why:
“Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When the Lord shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together.”

The Egyptians are men and not God, and their horses flesh and not spirit. The white man is just a man; he is not God, and their army has nothing on God's army. When the Lord stretches out his hand, the helper and the one he helps fall together. That is why we will remember the name of the Lord our God rather than trust in chariots and horses.
